diagnostic_workflow.overview:
This workflow guides systematic root cause analysis by integrating three critical diagnostic capabilities: Instana APM telemetry, OpenShift cluster diagnostics, and static code analysis. Follow this hypothesis-driven approach to identify and resolve production incidents efficiently.
CRITICAL DISTINCTION: - For metrics, services, and application data: ALWAYS use Instana MCP tools - For OpenShift cluster diagnostics: ONLY use when performing root cause analysis to correlate infrastructure state with Instana findings

phase.name: symptom_identification
phase.title: Phase 1: Identify Symptoms via Instana
phase.objective: Gather comprehensive observability data to understand the incident's scope, severity, and initial symptoms. This phase establishes the foundation for hypothesis formation.

step.data_to_collect: - Incident timeline and duration - Affected services and applications - Alert severity and frequency - Event state changes

step.metrics_to_examine: - Error rates and error types - Latency percentiles (P50, P90, P95, P99) - Request throughput and volume - Service dependencies and call patterns

step.infrastructure_checks: - JVM heap usage and GC activity - Container CPU and memory utilization - Database connection pool status - Message queue depths and processing rates

step.purpose: Identify slow spans, failed calls, and bottlenecks in the request path
step.look_for: - Abnormally slow database queries - Failed external API calls - Timeout errors - Retry storms

output.symptom_summary: Document the observed symptoms with specific metrics: - What is failing or degraded? - When did it start? - What is the impact (error rate, latency increase)? - Which services/components are affected?

phase.name: infrastructure_investigation
phase.title: Phase 2: Investigate OpenShift Cluster State (ROOT CAUSE ANALYSIS ONLY)
phase.objective:
IMPORTANT: This phase is ONLY used when performing root cause analysis.
When the user asks to "analyze root cause" or investigate an incident, correlate Instana symptoms with cluster-level events and resource states. Identify infrastructure or deployment issues that could be causing or contributing to the observed problems.
DO NOT use OpenShift commands for general metric queries or service listings. Those should ALWAYS come from Instana.

step.look_for: - Pod restarts (check RESTARTS column) - CrashLoopBackOff or ImagePullBackOff states - Pending pods (scheduling issues) - Terminating pods stuck in deletion

step.error_patterns: - OutOfMemoryError or OOMKilled - Connection refused or timeout errors - Stack traces and exceptions - Configuration errors

step.critical_events: - FailedScheduling (resource constraints) - Unhealthy (failed health checks) - BackOff (container startup failures) - FailedMount (volume issues)

step.resource_checks: - CPU throttling or saturation - Memory pressure or OOM conditions - Disk space exhaustion - Network bandwidth constraints

step.validation: - Correct environment variables - Valid connection strings - Proper secret mounting - Configuration version alignment

step.networking_checks: - Service selector matches pod labels - Endpoints are populated - Route TLS configuration - Load balancer health

correlation_analysis.guideline: Map cluster events to Instana incident timeline: - Do pod restarts align with error rate spikes? - Do OOMKills correlate with memory metrics? - Do deployment changes precede incidents? - Do resource constraints match performance degradation?

output.infrastructure_findings: Document cluster-level issues with evidence: - Specific pods/nodes affected - Resource constraint details - Configuration problems identified - Event timeline correlation with Instana

phase.name: code_analysis
phase.title: Phase 3: Static Code Analysis
phase.objective: Identify software defects, anti-patterns, or misconfigurations in the application code that could be causing the observed symptoms. Focus on areas implicated by Instana traces and OpenShift diagnostics.

step.search_targets: - Services/endpoints showing errors in Instana - Components with high latency in traces - Code paths leading to exceptions in logs - Configuration files referenced in errors

step.code_review_checklist: - Are exceptions properly caught and logged? - Are errors propagated correctly? - Are retry mechanisms implemented safely? - Are circuit breakers in place for external calls? - Are timeouts configured appropriately?

step.common_issues: - Unclosed database connections - Memory leaks (unbounded caches, listeners) - Thread pool exhaustion - File handle leaks - Inefficient object creation

step.performance_issues: - N+1 query problems - Missing indexes - Large result sets without pagination - Long-running transactions - Connection pool misconfiguration

step.concurrency_problems: - Race conditions - Deadlocks - Improper locking (too coarse or too fine) - Thread-unsafe shared state - Blocking operations on event loops

step.configuration_checks: - Environment-specific settings - Feature flags and toggles - Dependency version compatibility - Resource limits (heap size, thread pools) - Timeout and retry configurations

output.code_findings: Document code-level issues with specifics: - File paths and line numbers - Exact problematic code snippets - Explanation of why it's problematic - Link to symptoms observed in Instana/OpenShift

hypothesis_validation.principle: Form specific, testable hypotheses about the root cause based on evidence from all three phases. Systematically validate or refute each hypothesis.

hypothesis_template.hypothesis: Specific theory about what caused the incident
hypothesis_template.evidence_for: - Supporting data from Instana - Supporting data from OpenShift - Supporting data from code analysis
hypothesis_template.validation_test: How to definitively prove or disprove this hypothesis
hypothesis_template.conclusion: Confirmed, refuted, or needs more investigation

example_hypotheses.hypothesis: "Memory leak in caching layer causing OOMKills" - Evidence: Instana shows increasing heap usage, OpenShift shows OOMKilled pods, code shows unbounded cache without eviction policy
"Database connection pool exhaustion causing timeouts" - Evidence: Instana traces show connection timeout errors, OpenShift logs show "too many connections", code shows pool size too small for load
"Retry storm amplifying downstream failures" - Evidence: Instana shows exponential increase in error rate, traces show repeated retries, code shows aggressive retry without backoff

completion_criteria.criterion: Root cause identified with high confidence
Chain of causation from root cause to symptoms documented
Evidence from all three sources (Instana, OpenShift, code) correlated
Remediation steps defined with specific actions

escalation_triggers.trigger: Unable to access required Instana data or MCP tools
OpenShift cluster access issues or permission errors
Insufficient code access to validate hypotheses
Multiple conflicting hypotheses with equal evidence
Root cause requires architectural changes beyond immediate fix
